author: Alexiusimfight
quote:
I waited over a decade for this and got a lecture with a map attached. GTA was never supposed to be a morality play. You play a criminal, so let me be one.
If I want to put a bullet in someone, I want the freedom to go all the way. Instead the game keeps pulling its punches, as if it's embarrassed by its own premise. When I commit a crime, I want to actually pull it off properly, with real planning, real consequences and real payoff. What I got is scripted hand-holding with a cinematic bow on top.
The writing is the worst offender. The game constantly nudges me to feel sorry for people I'm meant to be robbing and shooting. I don't want empathy. I'm the bad guy and the game should let me enjoy it. The old games understood that and mocked everyone equally. This one picks a side and preaches from it, and the sermon is dull. The satire has no teeth left, just smug, progressive box-ticking that reads like it came out of a corporate workshop.
The pacing is padded to hell, too. Endless drives, pointless cutscenes and filler missions only exist to inflate the playtime. The plot starts big, loses track of itself and wraps up in a mess. Underneath the polish, the gameplay is a decade out of date.
